# Results -- Study 162 (Rosh-Hashanah)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Test: S&P 500 (^GSPC) daily
close-to-close return in the **Rosh Hashanah eve → Yom Kippur** window (~6-8 trading days,
~9 calendar days), 1980–2025, measured against matched random windows from the same calendar
month and against the unconditional 8-trading-day baseline. As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n obs | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC (Yahoo Finance, daily) | 1980-01-02 → 2026-06-12 | 11,707 daily closes | `9484879837bc` |
| Holiday event table | Hardcoded 1980–2026 (Reingold & Dershowitz 2018) | 47 years | (constant) |
| Usable windows | 1980–2025 | **46** | (both entry and exit in tape) |

## The honest test — holiday window return

*Entry: last trading day before Rosh Hashanah. Exit: first trading day on/after Yom Kippur.
Window typically 6–8 trading days.*

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| **n windows** | **46** (1980–2025) |
| **Mean return** | **−0.87 bps** |
| **Median return** | **−0.07 bps** |
| **% negative windows** | **50.0%** |
| **HAC t-stat (Newey-West)** | **−0.02** |
| Unconditional 8-trading-day S&P mean (all windows) | +33.2 bps |
| Gap vs unconditional | −34.1 bps |

**The HAC t-stat is −0.02 — a coin flip.** With annual S&P 500 volatility of ~16% and a
window of 6–8 trading days, one window's standard error is ≈ 240 bps. Detecting a real
−30 bps effect (the size of the unconditional gap) at 80% power with this noise level
would require roughly 260 years of data — far beyond our 46-year sample.

## The 2008 single-observation problem

The 2008 Yom Kippur window (2008-09-29 → 2008-10-09) coincided with the peak of the
Lehman Brothers crisis: S&P 500 fell **~17.76%** in those eight trading days, placing
this window at −1,776 bps — the most extreme observation in the dataset by a wide margin.

| Subsample | n | Mean (bps) | HAC t |
|---|---|---|---|
| All 1980–2025 | 46 | **−0.87** | −0.02 |
| Excluding 2008 | 45 | **+38.57** | +1.17 |
| 1980–1999 (pre-2000) | 20 | +63.36 | +1.12 |
| 2000–2025 (post-2000) | 26 | −50.28 | −0.81 |

Removing 2008 inverts the mean from −0.87 to +38.6 bps. **The entire measured "holiday
weakness" is one catastrophic year in which the Lehman crisis happened to fall during the
High Holiday window.** No subsample produces a HAC t exceeding |2.0|.

## Matched random-window comparison

For each holiday year, 40 random 8-trading-day windows were drawn from within ±21 calendar
days of Rosh Hashanah (excluding the holiday window itself). The holiday window was compared
to these matched controls:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Holiday mean − random median mean | **−11.54 bps** |
| HAC t-stat (gap) | **−0.17** |
| % years: holiday < matched random | 54.3% |

The holiday window is barely weaker than same-month random windows, with a t-stat of −0.17 —
not distinguishable from zero. The slight September seasonal that depresses both the holiday
and random windows is controlled away, and the residual holiday-specific gap is noise.

## Timing P&L — "Sell Rosh Hashanah, buy Yom Kippur"

Shorting the S&P 500 index at the entry close and buying back at the exit close, net of
5 bps per round-trip (two executions):

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Gross mean (= −window_ret) | +0.87 bps/window |
| Net of 5 bps round-trip (10 bps total) | **−9.13 bps/window** |
| HAC t-stat on net | **−0.22** |

Because the gross return is barely positive (effectively zero), trading costs make this a
certain loser on expectation. There is no break-even cost level.

## Synthetic positive control

The `data.synthetic_annual` generator confirms the detection machinery works: when a drag
of −100 bps/window is planted into 80 synthetic years, the HAC t recovers it as ≈ −5.4.
The real tape at −0.87 bps (HAC t = −0.02) is consistent with a world where no seasonal
effect exists or where the true effect is far smaller than the noise floor at n=46.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** HAC t = −0.02 on the raw window return. Gap vs matched random t = −0.17.
  No subsample (pre-2000, post-2000, excluding-2008) produces |t| > 2.0. The entire nominal
  "weakness" is 2008.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The timing gross is near zero; costs make it negative
  (t = −0.22 net). No break-even cost exists.
- **Third axis — Driven by 2008?: Yes.** Remove one observation and the mean inverts to
  +38.6 bps. This is not a seasonal; it is bad luck plus a small-n illusion.
